turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi, how are you doing right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Honestly, a little stressed, but okay.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My brother in law flips the board when he loses. He's forty two.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Oof. That kills the mood fast. Does it happen with every game, or certain kinds?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Mostly the ones where you attack each other.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then steer toward games with less direct conflict when he's there. Cooperative games or ones where everyone builds their own thing.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He'd say those are for babies.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Some really tough cooperative games would humble him quickly. Losing together to the game feels very different from losing to you.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ha. I like the idea of him

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: And it's fine to set a light house rule too, like whoever knocks the board does the washing up. Said with a smile, it usually works.
